item.title: Follow item cursors in inventory client
item.brief: Implement the client side of the approved shared cursor pagination contract. listItems(transport) must request all pages in order, send no cursor on first request, pass each returned next_cursor unchanged, and stop when next_cursor is null or absent. Update README documentation. Keep npm test passing. Commit the change.

item.title: Implement cursor pagination for GET /items
item.brief: Implement the API side of the approved shared cursor pagination contract. GET /items accepts optional limit (integer 1..100, default 20) and opaque cursor from prior response. Return ordered items and next_cursor string or null, null on last page. Invalid limit or cursor must return status 400 with JSON {"error":"..."}. Update README documentation. Keep python3 -m unittest passing. Commit the change.

evidence.caption: Before, GET /items returned 57 items with only the items key. After implementation, all six unittests pass, including paging through all 57 IDs in order.

pr.body: api.py encodes the last returned ID as a canonical URL-safe base64 cursor, validates limits and cursor values, and returns ordered pages with next_cursor. test_api.py covers default and bounded pages, full traversal, final-page behavior, and invalid parameters. README.md documents the contract. Assumption: cursors refer to IDs currently present in this in-memory catalogue. Verified with python3 -m unittest (6 tests, OK) and git diff --check.
pr.summary: Added bounded cursor pagination for GET /items. Clients can fetch ordered pages of up to 100 items and follow next_cursor; before: all 57 items came back in one response, now: default pages contain 20 items and end with a null cursor.
pr.title: Add cursor pagination to items endpoint
